text:
Elaine: Quick sync — a few enterprise customers asked for "customer-managed routing" in private deployments. They want control over egress/ingress routes and predictable upgrade paths. Can we scope this for Q2?

Jorge: Short answer: yes but we need to pick a level of support. Options: 1) static routes + docs, 2) iptables + helper scripts, 3) BGP peering + control plane hooks. Each has different ops surface.

Priya: Customer ask summary: two customers want BGP peering to propagate routes (finance and healthcare). Others just want the ability to specify NAT/external endpoints.

Samir: Implementation constraints: our private agent currently supports custom DNS and outbound proxy. Adding BGP requires FRRouting or similar in packaging + config templates. Also requires cert rotation considerations.

Elaine: Proposed MVP scope (opinion): static route templates + a "routing-mode" flag in agent config, plus clear upgrade contract for how route changes are applied. Defer BGP to M2 after we validate semantics with 2 customers.

Nina: Customers that asked for BGP are fine with pilot and a signed runbook. That suggests we can do a gated canary (dedicated pilot bundle) before full GA.

Jorge: Tech notes: example agent config (MVP):
```yaml
agent:
  routing_mode: static  # static | bgp (bgp behind feature flag)
  static_routes:
    - cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
      next_hop: 192.168.1.1
  egress_proxy: proxy.company.local:3128
```
We can wire this into the init script and netplan/iptables templates.

Priya: Upgrade path concerns: customers need predictable ordering and rollback if route updates break connectivity. Suggest we require an explicit "apply window" and health-check probe that can rollback within 2 minutes.

Samir: Agreed. Also need to expose a dry-run mode that prints intended iptables/netplan diffs. Many netops teams will want that.

Elaine: Launch criteria for MVP: 1) docs + config reference, 2) two pilot customers validate apply/rollback, 3) we ship dry-run and audit logs, 4) SLO for upgrade success rate >= 95% in pilot.

Jorge: Risks: packaging size increases if we bundle FRR; complexity for air-gapped installs. Mitigations: use feature-flagged optional package and provide prebuilt offline bundle.

Nina: Operational asks from customers: 1) clear changelog for route-affecting releases, 2) ability to opt-out of automatic upgrades for the agent during pilot.

Elaine: Next steps: - Eng to prototype static-route flow + dry-run by EOD next week (Jorge/Samir) - Product to draft pilot success criteria and runbook (Elaine/Priya) - Customer success to identify pilot contacts and sign runbook (Nina)

Jorge: I'll post a short PR with the config schema and a sample Ansible task.

deploy-bot: Scheduled pipeline for private-agent:build-rc-217 triggered by @Jorge (ci link: https://ci.redwood.example/217) :gear:

Priya: One more note — telemetry: we must not send routing tables to hosted telemetry (PII/regulatory). Ensure telemetry only emits hashes and success/failure signals.

Elaine: Good call. I'll add telemetry constraints to the PR checklist. Thanks all. :rocket:
